DispatchHold.description: Ledger-wide admission condition, projected only onto Runs waiting to submit. Never a Run outcome.

restore_operation_revision.description: When present, acknowledges a committed fresh RevokeAll for this restore operation. Omitted for general or legacy revocation.

computer_attempt_id.description: When present, acknowledges a committed revocation of only this attempt's grants.

committed_at.description: L3 audit time; never a cross-host ordering prerequisite.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code; shared HTTP codes are open vocabulary. L1 operational Fabric identity lookup failures return HTTP 503 unavailable, retryable=true, details.reason=identity_unverifiable; genuine absence remains HTTP 401 unauthorized. CLI transport failures (including request deadlines and a deadline or timeout waiting for the take-over display banner after WebSocket upgrade) and non-envelope HTTP 5xx use unavailable with retryable=true and exit 13, including Computer take-over front-door responses to view open, take, and release (such as plain-text 503 display-not-ready or identity-unverifiable failures). The unavailable message retains the front door plain-text reason, bounded to 4096 response bytes. Structured take-over refusals, including HTTP 5xx on view open, take, and release, preserve the server code, message, retryability, details, request ID and any receipt; view open adds the HTTP status to the message. The CLI exit map still applies: tenure_unavailable exits 1 even when retryable, without being rewritten to internal or transport unavailable. A plain-text or structured 401 authentication refusal exits 3. HTTP 5xx envelopes with retryable internal or run_ledger_unavailable also exit 13 while retaining the server code; non-retryable versions remain exit 1. Bare local deadlines and caller cancellation (including Ctrl-C during take-over or registry requests) are not unavailable; cancellation remains exit 1. Accepted-mutation observation timeouts use the CLI-local wait_timeout code, retryable=false, and exit 14; this is not a server error code. details.mutation_applied is always present: true or false from the Computer receipt (false for replay/no-op), and always null for service lifecycle/removal because L1 provides no applied receipt for desired-state or remove mutations; a prior read cannot prove application under a concurrent change. Null means applied evidence is unknown. services revoke --wait also exits 14 on revocation_wait_timeout, retaining that code, retryability, and receipt-derived applied evidence.

retryable.description: Advises whether repeating the same request may succeed. A known authority-loss code always governs the caller's reaction.

details.description: For stale_intent_revision (HTTP 409, retryable=false), expected_revision is the current stored intent revision and observed_revision is the revision supplied by the caller. Details also carry the resource identifier (node_id or computer_id). L1 operational identity lookup failures carry reason=identity_unverifiable (503 unavailable, retryable=true). On dispatch-key lookup, Computer token-scope proof, and host boot-session proof, refusal of a client that is not the configured run ledger carries reason=run_ledger_not_admitted (403 forbidden, retryable=false); per-Computer and per-host authority refusals retain their existing details without that reason. Mux 404/405 errors carry reason=no_route to distinguish missing routes or methods from resource refusals.

request_id.description: Server-generated HTTP request correlation ID, echoed in X-Request-Id and the server log. L3 preserves a relayed L1 error ID and adds its own ID in details.l3_request_id and X-L3-Request-Id. Omitted for CLI-local and stored decision errors that have no HTTP request.

JobSpec.description: Open-kind workload contract. kind=process uses the flat process execution fields; handoff_directory is optional for one-shots, whose omitted path assigns managed output owned by the server-assigned Job ID unless run labels name an owner; explicit absolute paths without run labels remain unowned; kind=oci uses execution.oci while env and sensitive_env remain shared. An OCI one-shot without run labels owns its helper-managed handoff by the server-assigned Job ID, with result capture before reap and L1 result upload requiring no L3. Explicit run identities keep their entitlement and owner semantics; fallback ownership never rewrites labels or the request hash. execution.oci.computer is an optional trait valid only on digest-pinned, Pinned OCI service Jobs; it adds no kind, class, state, or scheduling axis. Optional instance_key reserves at most one live job in the authenticated Fabric submitter namespace. Keys are 1-255 visible ASCII characters, case-sensitive, with identity normalization (no trimming or folding); omission is unkeyed, empty and null are invalid. One-shots release on terminal state; services retain through stopped, failed and removal until ordinary-row deletion. Computers cannot carry instance_key.

JobRecordSpec.description: A Job's stored spec as a response returns it: the JobSpec contract, except that execution.executable may be a scrubbed record. A terminal one-shot's inline script bytes are removed with its secrets (see Job.secrets_scrubbed_at); its sha256, interpreter and mode stay. This is its own schema resource, so its widened executable applies only beneath it: a submitted JobSpec is always held to path or inline_base64.

anyOf.description: Scrubbed inline executable: the bytes are gone and the sha256 records what ran.

computer_id.description: Durable Computer authority owning this immutable Job projection, when present.

node_id.description: Stable node ID for the current or latest attempt. This is not the durable service binding.

status.description: Computed operator projection. Either class may be unschedulable while persisted state remains queued; restart-pending is service-only.

spec.description: Absent after removal finalizes; tombstones retain no executable or environment bytes. Once secrets_scrubbed_at is set it is the permanent record of a terminal one-shot, not a resubmittable request: execution.executable keeps its sha256, interpreter and mode but no inline_base64 (JobRecordSpec), and the run_params_json label is gone. Without secrets_scrubbed_at the spec is a full JobSpec. Client responses never carry sensitive_env.

outcome.description: Job-level cancellation decision, independent of any attempt process result. Reserved at accepted cancellation. An active process or OCI one-shot retains its current state until completion, lease loss, or the fixed 30-second settlement deadline makes it failed; renewal cannot extend settlement. Logical cancellation never proves runtime termination. A never-claimed canceled job has no attempts or signal; a requeued job retains its earlier attempt evidence.

allowed_actions.description: Service caller projections, including removal tombstones: start, stop, restart, remove, forget. Same actor-aware decision as writes. start/stop require exact desired_state; restart requires a caller-chosen idempotency_key input; forget requires force=true. No service revision guard or service grants exist. Active and retired Computer-owned Job projections refuse these Job verbs with computer_resource_required. During Computer removal, start, stop and restart refuse with not_found because the mutable service row is absent; remove and forget still refuse with computer_resource_required. One-shots omit this field.

last_condition.description: Service reads only: closest persisted policy_stop, failure_latched, never_automatic_restart_suppressed, or removal phase, using existing state-machine timestamps. Null when none applies. Restart conditions use the current attempt update timestamp when retained, otherwise the Job timestamp; unrelated Job updates such as stop do not advance a retained attempt condition. Reads do not advance since or fabricate event history. One-shots omit this field.

parent_job_id.description: Job whose live attempt submitted this job through its attempt credential. Derived from the credential, never supplied by the caller; absent on a root job.

parent_attempt_id.description: Exact parent attempt that submitted this job. Absent on a root job.

originating_submitter.description: Stable Fabric node ID of the client principal that created the root job. Inherited unchanged by every descendant and never widened.

spawn_depth.description: Number of parent links above this job. Zero for a root job; a submission past the fixed cap of 8 is refused with spawn_depth_exceeded.

attempts.description: Retained operator-safe attempt summaries in chronological order. Write-authority fields are never exposed.

desired_state.description: Service jobs only. Requested lifecycle target, distinct from observed state.

bound_node_id.description: Service jobs only. Durable service binding, retained independently of node_id.

node_state.description: Service jobs only. Current liveness of the bound node.

holds_slot.description: Service jobs only. Whether the binding currently occupies one service slot.

unschedulable_reason.description: Present for either class when execution capabilities prevent claim; service jobs may additionally name binding, liveness, intent, routing, or capacity facts.

failure_reason.description: Present when L1 terminalized a job without minting a new attempt, such as expiry of a persisted pre-start infrastructure budget while awaiting scheduling.

secrets_scrubbed_at.description: One-shot jobs only. When L1 removed the job's sensitive environment, inline executable bytes and run_params_json label from its stored spec, in the same transaction that made it succeeded or failed. Absent while the job can still run.

policy_stop.description: Ordinary service only. A clean payload exit under on-failure or never, or a payload failure (nonzero exit, spontaneous signal, restartable readiness failure) under never. Agent/guardian-requested termination, runtime loss and lease loss are infrastructure, never a policy stop. Clean exit observes stopped; never payload failure observes failed; both release capacity without restart accounting. It suppresses automatic claims without changing desired_state. An explicit start or restart clears it, and so does the image-reconciliation failure latch, which records its own last_failure. An operator stop keeps it, so a later start still clears it.

restart_suppressed_reason.description: Present when durable desired state, a policy stop, or a failed state suppresses automatic restart. An automatically-failed never service names its current attempt cause (lease loss, agent or guardian interruption from the stored termination initiator or signal cause, or infrastructure completion) and may resume by explicit start or restart; terminal latches retain precedence. A payload's own exit code or spontaneous signal claimed by an explicit restart is never an interruption: at max_restart_streak both name the streak limit and accept restart only.

lease_loss_count.description: Service jobs only. Attempts whose lease expired. A lease loss proves execution authority ended, not that the process failed, so it is counted apart from restarts and drives its own bounded retry backoff when requeue is permitted. Under never, loss after durable OCI Started or process start acknowledgement leaves failed without a restart timer, policy_stop or last_failure; legacy process renewal promotion is not start evidence. Pre-start loss retains existing rules; explicit restart for the exact attempt permits requeue.

published_port.description: Service jobs only. Ready publication endpoint; absent unless ready is true. The immutable requested port remains in spec.published_port.

ready.description: Portful service jobs only. True only while the current attempt has active authoritative publication; omitted for portless services.

last_failure.description: Service failure evidence: a bare SpawnFailure for a spawn/readiness failure, otherwise the ProcessResult. A suppressed post-start never infrastructure completion records its fact here without a policy stop or restart accounting. Lease loss fabricates no result and preserves earlier failure evidence; its current cause is named in restart_suppressed_reason. A readiness policy_stop always carries the full ProcessResult including spawn_error.

cleanup_acknowledged_at.description: Present only when a bound agent attested deletion. A verified unbound removal omits it because no managed resource ever existed.

stalled_at.description: Present only for removal_outcome cleanup_stalled: when L1 accepted the bound agent's declaration and released the service slot.

admins.description: Present only for a current administrator.

revocations.description: Per-Computer revocations created by an administrator removal. Each remains pending until its current node boot acknowledges installation after matching sessions close.

AdminPolicy.description: Current bounded person-based administrator policy. Membership is scoped to the issuing Fabric; device identity is audit evidence, never membership.

AuthenticatedPerson.description: The caller person identity authenticated by Fabric. Calling this route records the stable FabricID/UserID pair as grantable person evidence; DeviceID remains audit evidence.

ComputerGrant.description: Current person grant scoped to its issuing Fabric. none is durable revocation, never absence or fallback.

mutation_applied.description: True when this request committed the mutation and its new policy revision; false on an idempotent replay.

ComputerPolicySnapshot.description: Short-lived issuing-Fabric/L1-generation/Node/boot-bound policy. Agents keep it only in memory and fail closed on loss, expiry, or any revision below the cache high-water mark.

ComputerPolicyInstallAcknowledgement.description: Assertion-derived receipt emitted from installed memory only after every affected authorization lease releases.

ComputerTakeoverAuditEvent.description: Immutable identity/policy evidence only. Display data, input data, endpoints, and fencing tokens are forbidden. Every session opens in view; controller events are emitted only by the session-bound Controller-tenure contract.

ComputerTakeoverAuditList.description: Chronological immutable take-over evidence with no credentials, endpoints, display data, input data, or fencing material.

ComputerTakeoverSession.description: Session evidence derived from immutable open/close and Controller-tenure audit rows. open_without_close may briefly lag a live close because close audit finalization follows the socket boundary.

ComputerTakeoverAccess.description: Person-bound view-first discovery. friendly_name is the wefty-owned Computer name. The endpoint is the authorized Fabric front door, never a raw view/control backend; null means admission is not ready. Discovery is durable availability, never a live admission role: the front door always attempts view-first admission at the agent's current evaluator. On that private endpoint and its sideband take/release paths, genuine Fabric identity absence returns HTTP 401; operational identity lookup failures return HTTP 503 with generic text, without the cause or diagnostic category, before any grant, session, or backend dial.

ComputerHandleResolution.description: Person-authorized CLI handle resolution. Exact computer_id wins, then current_job_id, then the UNIQUE friendly name.

bound_node_id.description: Durable service binding. Stop releases only Slot occupancy and retains this binding.

backup_cap.description: Effective retained Backup cap. Zero disables creation; pruning is always explicit.

restore_operation.description: Present only when the read named a restore_operation_revision: that restore's own state.

clone_operation.description: Present only when the read named a clone_operation_revision: that clone's own state.

owed_revocations.description: Explicit L3 revocations this Computer's authority-losing mutations committed and the run ledger has not yet taken, oldest first. Omitted when none is owed. L3's live-scope check already refuses the old passes; each settles on the host Node's heartbeat, attempt-scoped (#554).

storage_cleanup_quarantines.description: All unresolved typed cleanup quarantines across removal, reset, and restore operations; no operation shadows another.

removal_outcome.description: Computer-only custody outcome. removed_reduced proves managed cleanup while another clone branch still bears the secret.

display_endpoint.description: Private take-over front-door endpoint. Null until the admission module is active; never a placeholder URL.

controller_tenure.description: Current Controller-tenure truth derived from immutable current-attempt audit evidence.

allowed_actions.description: Client Computer verbs evaluated for this authenticated caller. Person-only grants, submission and take-over are omitted; agent-only callers receive refused client verbs. Describes new operations with valid inputs, not replay keys or same-image reimage no-ops. Backup verbs require at least one valid status=available Backup choice; pruned and pruning records are excluded. With no available choice, caller and resource checks precede not_found. A corrupt available choice is skipped when another choice succeeds; with no success, any internal choice refusal takes precedence.

last_condition.description: Latest recorded intent, grow or Backup completion, or removal stall from existing evidence. Recording time is preserved on reads; null when no evidence exists.

Computer.description: Durable Computer identity and sole desired-state authority. computer_id and current_job_id are distinct; immutable Job projections cannot be restarted after retirement.

ComputerList.description: One stable page of durable Computer authorities. Terminal removal truth remains listed.

copy_receipt.description: Present only in the storage-provenance projection, on restore, clone, and import entries: the verified helper receipt that published the destination generation.

custody_tainted.description: True when the custody graph contains imported external bytes or a Custody export that may have placed bytes outside managed custody. An export the helper refused before touching the destination (managed_root_path, external_path_unconfined, external_root_unmounted, or external_path_crosses_mount) does not taint. Operator deletion attestation never clears it.

os_identity_rekeyed.description: Clone and import only: the destination's machine-id was rekeyed. Nothing else in the OS identity is rewritten.

machine_id_before_digest.description: Clone and import only: digest of the copied machine-id before rekeying.

machine_id_after_digest.description: Clone and import only: digest of the destination machine-id after rekeying; it differs from machine_id_before_digest.

machine_id_repaired.description: Clone and import only: the copied machine-id was not well-formed and the helper repaired it before rekeying.

source_unchanged.description: The helper re-verified the source after the copy. True on every verified receipt, false on failed_absent.

destination_prepared.description: The destination disk carries its preparation marker. True on every verified receipt, false on failed_absent.

preparation_receipt.description: The destination disk carries a Storage-reset preparation receipt. Always false: a copied destination is never a reset generation.

destination_chown.description: The destination requested an ownership rewrite. Always false for a Storage copy.

failure_code.description: failed_absent receipts only. Custody import may report any of these; clone reports only insufficient_disk; restore has no failure receipt.

observed_available_bytes.description: The capacity fact behind an insufficient_disk refusal, measured on the Node when the copy was refused. Absent from every other outcome and when zero.

ComputerStorageCopyReceipt.description: Assertion-derived helper evidence that one exact Backup copy produced a detached destination Storage generation (verified), or that a refused copy left no staged destination behind (failed_absent). The source digest is checked before any destination publication; the destination digest is recorded after the machine-id rekey and optional expansion.

ComputerStoragePreparationOutcome.description: Generation-bound reason why a Custody import destination is not currently preparable. Runtime-loss observations are agent-authored from typed helper generation evidence; sweep fields are present when the outcome came from durable startup-recovery inventory.

ComputerCustodyImportObservation.description: Durable revision-bound observation used by services custody import --wait.

encryption.description: V1 fact: Wefty adds no Backup encryption layer.

operation.description: Present only when the request named a backup_id: that operation's own state.

ComputerBackupOperationOutcome.description: Computer Backup operation observation. A planned status is still running and every other status is terminal: published succeeded; failed always carries a typed failure_code; superseded means a removal or dead-node abort overtook it. A superseded operation carries completed_at only once its planned copy's absence is recorded, so a caller judges the outcome by status, not by completed_at.

ComputerStorageGrowOutcome.description: Latest durable Computer Storage grow observation. Available bytes exist only when a validated helper refusal receipt supplied them.

ComputerRestoreOperation.description: One Computer restore's own observed state. `retired` completed it; `failed` means the precommitted predecessor Backup copy failed and the restore was aborted with the old generation still current, and carries that copy's failure_code; `superseded` means a removal overtook it. The Computer is `stable` after both `retired` and `failed`.

ComputerCloneOperation.description: One Computer clone's own observed state, read through its destination Computer. reserved and prepared are still running; complete published the destination generation; failed means the helper refused the destination or could never prepare it and carries failure_code; superseded means a removal of the destination or source overtook it. The destination's Job failure may belong to a later operation, so only this record says how the clone ended.

ServiceRemovalStall.description: Operator projection of an agent-declared stalled removal. It records only non-completion and asserts no deletion. Cleanup authority is deliberately absent: the cleanup fence and boot session that produced the declaration grant write authority and explain nothing about the failure.

phase.description: Durable runtime-removal phase the removal had reached.

last_refusal_code.description: Typed code of the refusal the cleanup kept receiving.

attempts.description: Consecutive cleanup attempts that produced this same typed refusal.

ServiceRemovalStallEvidence.description: The bound agent's declaration that a runtime removal cannot complete. Valid only for kind=oci services and Computers, the only removals a helper can refuse with a typed code. It carries no boot session: the agent freezes these exact bytes before the first send and replays them until L1 accepts them, so the declaration must stay valid across the restart a lost response can straddle, while the enclosing request proves the current boot.

ComputerStorageCleanupQuarantine.description: Authority-bound terminal evidence that bounded Computer-disk cleanup exhausted three attempts. The owning operation remains pending and must not be redispatched as ordinary cleanup.

host_node_id.description: The Node whose heartbeat settles this revocation.

scope.description: What the revocation sent right after the mutation ends: every grant of the Computer, or exactly computer_attempt_id's. A late settlement is always attempt-scoped, one request per recorded attempt, and never sends a revoke-all.

recorded_attempt_ids.description: The attempts whose passes this revocation ends: those of the Computer's current Job that were claimed or running when the mutation began, or the one completed attempt. An attempt started later is never named, so a late settlement cannot touch it.

revoked_attempt_ids.description: Recorded attempts the run ledger has already revoked; the row settles when every recorded attempt is here.

OwedComputerRevocation.description: An explicit L3 revocation an authority-losing Computer mutation committed in its own transaction and the run ledger has not yet taken (#554).

ComputerRestoreRevocationReceipt.description: Restore-attributable proof that L1 requested RevokeAll and L3 durably revoked prior Computer token grants before successor attachment. Take-over session termination is attempt-lineage-bound and is evidenced separately by takeover_session_ended.

superseded.description: True only when irreversible Computer removal superseded a stale create before helper-side absence proof.

fencing_token.description: Opaque monotonically increasing per-job fence; never parse as a number.

lease_expires_at.description: Compatibility wall-clock expiry. Agents use lease_ttl after the resilience cutover.

lease_ttl.description: Granted lease duration in nanoseconds. The agent measures it from its monotonic request start, without comparing clocks.

directive.description: Attempt-scoped intent: stop/restart for services, cancel for process and OCI one-shots. Cancel uses TERM, a five-second grace, then KILL. Omission means no lifecycle change is requested.

through_sequence.description: Inclusive last sequence covered by this per-stream gap. LogEvent.sequence is the first covered sequence.

source_event_sha256.description: Present when L1 replaces an out-of-window event with a gap so exact replay remains distinguishable from conflicting payloads.

LogGap.description: A truthful declaration that raw log events from exactly one stream are unavailable. A source event larger than the entire service spool budget is converted whole into one oversized_event gap; it is not partially retained or chunked at eviction time.

bytes.description: One non-empty raw byte chunk, up to 4 MiB before base64 encoding. Chunks are not lines: values may exceed 64 KiB, end with a partial line, or contain invalid UTF-8. Ordering is guaranteed per attempt and stream only.

LogEvent.description: One ordered raw chunk or gap declaration. Continuity and gap ranges are independent for stdout and stderr.

bound_kind.description: The retention bound that most recently caused eviction: the job's per-job byte cap (bytes), its class's age bound measured by each event's own timestamp (age), or the cluster-wide ceiling on all jobs' logs (total). Clients should treat an unknown value as a truncation of unknown cause, not an error.

evicted_through_ordinal.description: Internal monotonic ordering watermark; clients must not use it as a reader cursor.

earliest_retained_at.description: Timestamp of the oldest event still retained; null when every event was evicted.

LogTruncation.description: One aggregate L1 history-truncation marker per job, one-shot or service: retained log history was evicted by a retention bound and the bytes are deleted. Counts only grow. A trimmed job carries it on every page, so trimmed logs never read as empty ones. This is distinct from LogGap, which declares loss before L1 accepted evidence.

ServiceLogTruncation.description: Pre-#52 name of LogTruncation, kept so existing references resolve. The wire shape is identical.

output_error.description: Output redaction, durable spooling, or upload finalization failed for a reason other than the bounded log-finalization deadline; the process exit code is not authoritative success.

termination_cause.description: Structured initiator for a signal termination; never infer intent from signal or error strings.

oom.description: Additive runtime evidence. It does not select a primary result arm and is never inferred from exit 137.

disk_exhausted.description: Additive runtime evidence that the helper positively observed ENOSPC for this Computer attempt. It is absent when no authoritative write-budget or filesystem error event is available and is never inferred from free-byte samples, stderr, or an exit code.

log_evidence_incomplete.description: Additive evidence alongside one valid primary arm that a helper log segment was lost, corrupt, or truncated, or that the bounded agent log-finalization deadline expired after a payload result. It is not attached to a pre-Started OCI spawn_error.

code.description: Stable machine-readable spawn failure code. Unknown codes default to terminal service policy.
Stable post-Started runtime failure code. Unknown codes default terminal.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor; clients must not infer SQLite row IDs.

ResultUploadSkipReason.description: Why a finished run has no result document here. The set is closed: a reason is an answer a person acts on, not free text a node invents. A node normally uploads nothing at all for "absent" -- the run wrote no result -- and uploads one of the others when a result exists on the node and could not travel.

document.description: The run's own result.json, byte for byte, at most 1 MiB. Exactly one of document or skip_reason is sent.

sha256.description: Optional digest of document, checked when present so a truncated upload is refused rather than stored.

status.description: The run's status, from the same vocabulary as RunRecord.status.

trigger.description: The Run's immutable trigger provenance, the same projection RunRecord carries.

current_step.description: Where the Run is now; empty for a Run in no step.

RunListPage.description: The general Run listing, ordered by creation time then Run ID descending. next_cursor is present only when another page exists; resume with the same status and submitting actor scope. Inserts newer than the cursor do not shift subsequent pages. Status is evaluated at each request, not snapshotted.

NodeRegistration.description: The registration request: exactly NodeRegistrationFields and nothing else.

connect_host.description: Fabric-produced hostname for combining with a published port. Descriptive only; never an identity, authorization, or scheduling input.

root_instance_id.description: Self-reported identity of the node's current agent-owned managed resource root. Descriptive only; never an eligibility or scheduling input.

capabilities.description: Node-advertised execution facts such as kind:process, kind:oci, runtime_handler:<name>, and cgroup_v2. Operators separately own routing tags and class-scoped capacity; max_oneshot_slots and max_service_slots are reserved control-plane policy keys and are rejected.

capability_revision.description: Boot-scoped monotonic revision over the complete capability observation.

capability_reason_code.description: Closed capability restriction reason. Native Linux and Lima boot barriers use the same typed helper failure classification. helper_unreachable means a helper connection could not be established, including a sweep or verification RPC connection after session admission. helper_handshake_failed means the helper handshake or session admission failed. boot_sweep_failed means namespace residue remains or another sweep or verification failure occurred. helper_unit_unavailable means the helper socket unit remained absent or refused connections throughout takeover; helper_handshake_stalled means takeover connected but did not complete handshake or admission; helper_handshake_stalled_persistent means that stall persisted through the recovery deadline. helper_version_mismatch means the helper protocol version or checksum differs from the expected value; local_permission_denied means local permissions or helper peer authentication prevented access.

supersede_capability_revision.description: Asks L1 to assign the stored capability_revision + 1 to this restrictive same-boot observation atomically. Reserved for a runtime authority barrier that must revoke stale advertised capability before it can learn the stored revision.

NodeRegistrationFields.description: No tags or capacity fields are accepted. Operators own routing tags and class-scoped slot policy; the node advertises one complete boot-revisioned execution capability observation. connect_host is a non-authoritative Fabric projection. Open on purpose: NodeRegistration, Node, and HeartbeatResponse compose it and close at their own level with unevaluatedProperties, since a closed member inside allOf would refuse its siblings' fields.

chown.description: One-shot ownership migration authority for the current reimage projection.

requires.description: Exact request field/value preconditions only, keyed by literal request JSON names (for example intent_revision: 7). Copy these pairs into the body. Never caller-chosen input descriptors. Omitted or {} when empty, never null. A field occurs in either requires or inputs, never both.

inputs.description: Caller-chosen request fields. Omitted or [] when empty, never null. Endpoint schemas constrain chosen values.

AllowedAction.description: Shared unchanged by Nodes, services and Computers. Evaluated for the authenticated actor and resource snapshot. refused_because is omitted only when the decision passes with valid chosen inputs and exact preconditions; any error refuses, using the same scrubbing and retryability as a write. Writes recheck the same actor-aware predicates atomically. Refusals are facts, never recommendations.

name.description: Literal request field or path parameter name.

in.description: Where to send a caller-chosen value. Omitted means body; path means substitute the URL parameter.

type.description: JSON type of the caller's value.

required.description: Whether the caller must supply the field, never a required value.

Condition.description: Last recorded notable fact, retained through ordinary heartbeats and reads. Open code and scope vocabularies; since is the control-plane recording time, not a guarantee that the condition still holds.

NodeActiveAttempt.description: Nonterminal persisted attempt on this Node, including prior boots until reconciled. Read routes reconcile expiry first. Reports execution state and lease, never a credential, fence or proof that a payload is physically running.

Node.description: The Node factual projection: exactly NodeFields and nothing else. Client and agent routes evaluate allowed_actions for their real authenticated caller; agent-only callers have no operator action authority.

NodeFields.description: NodeRegistrationFields plus L1's authoritative Node facts. Open on purpose so HeartbeatResponse can extend it; Node closes it.

oneshot_occupancy.description: Current one-shot slot occupancy from non-terminal one-shot attempts.

service_occupancy.description: Current service slot occupancy from durable service bindings.

overcommitted.description: True when either class occupancy exceeds its effective configured limit; resident workloads are not killed.

authority_generation.description: Monotonic registration generation bound into new attempts.

claims_enabled.description: Durable operator intent controlling admission of new claims.

last_condition.description: Null for upgraded Nodes with no recorded condition; historical conditions are never invented. Capability reason clearing records node_capability_recovered in node_capability scope, with stored capability_revision and missing_capabilities. Repeated observations preserve since.

allowed_actions.description: Computed at the route for the real authenticated caller through the write decision. drain requires exact intent_revision and claims_enabled=false, plus required string input reason. set-claims requires exact intent_revision, plus required string reason and boolean claims_enabled inputs; either boolean value is legal. Both are independent of liveness. Agent-only principals are refused with principal_forbidden, matching client write routes.

OneShotCancelDirective.description: Standing stop delivery for one process or OCI one-shot, fenced by job, attempt, fence and heartbeat boot session. Persists after logical settlement until attempt completion evidence is recorded. Receipt of this directive is not confirmed runtime termination.

one_shot_cancel_directives.description: Boot- and authority-generation-scoped one-shot cancellation. Match the resident attempt and fence, then use TERM, grace, KILL and normal finalization. An absent resident is a no-op.

removal_directives.description: Boot-session-scoped standing cleanup directives, including when no attempt is live.

storage_reset_directives.description: Revision-fenced standing work that must verify old-generation deletion before the replacement generation can publish.

storage_grow_directives.description: Revision- and managed-root-fenced grow work. The current Storage generation and running attempt remain authoritative until a positive applied receipt is accepted.

reimage_preflight_directives.description: Identity-, managed-root-, and revision-fenced work that verifies target image platform, image user and detached disk ownership before reimage publication.

backup_directives.description: Planned source-node copies released only after the Computer is quiesced.

backup_prune_directives.description: Explicit physical copy removals requiring positive absence receipts.

storage_copy_directives.description: Restore and clone work released only from a published source-node Backup copy; published restore rows remain until predecessor absence is acknowledged.

custody_export_directives.description: Transfers released only after L1 durably records permanent external custody taint.

computer_policy.description: Heartbeat bootstrap only. Fast changes and freshness renewal use the policy watch. Omitted for nodes that have never hosted a Computer.

RunRecord.description: The ledger RunRecord. CLI wait JSON preserves recorded failure_reason; for a failed legacy Run without one, the CLI includes a reason derived from a bounded execution-evidence lookup when available, without mutating the ledger.

RequestId.description: Matches error.request_id; generated by this server, or preserved from an upstream L1 error.

L3RequestId.description: L3 only: independently generated local request ID, also present in details.l3_request_id when relaying an L1 error.

Unauthorized.description: Authentication failed. L1 returns 401 unauthorized with retryable=false for genuine Fabric identity absence; operational identity lookup failure is instead 503 unavailable.

Forbidden.description: The authenticated principal is outside its scope.

Conflict.description: State, fence, lease, dispatch key, or idempotency conflict.

UnprocessableEntity.description: Syntactically valid contract data cannot be executed, such as an unsupported kind.

NotImplemented.description: Reserved contract surface. Always returns code not_implemented and retryable false in v0.1.

Unavailable.description: L1 could not verify Fabric identity because lookup failed operationally: unavailable, retryable=true, details.reason=identity_unverifiable. Applies to every L1 authenticated protocol, including person, cancel, and attempt credentials. The cause is logged safely server-side and never included in the response. Safe log categories include issuing_fabric_unavailable for missing issuing Fabric configuration and identity_incomplete for missing stable peer identity fields; these are diagnostics only and do not change this response.

fabricIdentity.description: Identity supplied by the selected Fabric implementation. Person-policy routes require opaque stable UserID and DeviceID; display data is never authority.
